title: Against Celsus, Book VIII
blurb: Celsus urges Christians to honour the demons as servants of the one God, to share in the public feasts and sacrificial meals, and to support the emperor by oath, office and military service. Origen answers that no one can serve two masters, that Christians keep a feast to God at all times and honour Him in living temples, and that they help the emperor most by their prayers and serve their country by governing the churches.
first_english_note: Earlier English: Frederick Crombie (Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1872) and Henry Chadwick (1953). This is a fresh English translation from Koetschau's Greek; neither was used as wording.

text_history.method: Translated from the Greek of Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI, which serves as the copy-text. Each chapter was translated from the Greek and then checked clause by clause against it: chapters 1–75 in an independent review, the closing chapter 76 in the translator's own second pass. No earlier English translation was consulted.
